(c) Find the particular solution \(y=f(x)\) to the given differential equation with initial condition \(f(1)=0\).

\item[(c)] \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{1}{3} x(y-2)^{2}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \int \frac{d y}{(y-2)^{2}}=\int \frac{1}{3} x d x \\
& \frac{-1}{y-2}=\frac{1}{6} x^{2}+C \\
& \frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{6}+C \Rightarrow C=\frac{1}{3} \\
& \frac{-1}{y-2}=\frac{1}{6} x^{2}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{x^{2}+2}{6} \\
& y=2-\frac{6}{x^{2}+2}
\end{aligned}
\]
Note: this solution is valid for \(-\infty<x<\infty\).
